column1: # clues.tsv for ft.h — hints only, never answers.
# (Single member-less hint: this exercise's failure is one compile, not a table.)

The failure you are reading comes from compiling a test file you did not write, against your header. That is the point of the exercise: someone else's code has to build on the strength of your ft.h alone. Two questions. First, does the header carry a prototype for every one of the five functions the subject lists, spelled exactly as the subject spells them — same return type, same parameter types? A prototype that differs in any of those is not the same declaration. Second, what stops a header from being safe to #include twice in one build? Look up what an include guard is and what the three preprocessor lines that make one are called; the Norm also has an opinion about how the lines inside a header are indented.
